1.explanation:
1. lighthouse-cli/printer.ts: This CLI printer formats and logs all audit metrics and summary values. It currently uses manual rounding (e.g. toFixed) and string concatenation. It should use toLocaleString(undefined, opts) to produce thousands separators and controlled decimals.
2. lighthouse-cli/performance-experiment/report/perf-x-report-generator.js: The performance experiment report generator emits numeric results (e.g. histograms, percentiles). These values are turned into strings via manual formatting; switching to toLocaleString will unify output.
3. lighthouse-core/report/formatter.js: Responsible for orchestrating how raw audit data is turned into human-readable strings in HTML reports. It contains number formatting logic that needs replacing with locale-aware calls.
4. lighthouse-core/report/handlebar-helpers.js: Defines Handlebars helpers (formatNumber, formatBytes, etc.) used in templates. These helpers perform string manipulation on numbers and should delegate to toLocaleString for consistent locale formatting.
1.bug_scenario: The repository currently outputs numeric values (metrics, diagnostics, byte sizes, experiment data, etc.) by manually rounding or concatenating numbers—often using toFixed or string concatenation—resulting in outputs like “2445.8”, “2445”, or “2445.01” without locale-aware thousands separators. The bug report demonstrates that Number.prototype.toLocaleString can handle both decimal precision and thousands separators in one step, producing outputs like “2,445.8” or “2,445”. We need to adopt toLocaleString across all consumer code so that every number output honors the user’s locale and desired fractional precision.

2.explanation:
All of the user-facing number formatting in Lighthouse flows through these four modules:

• lighthouse-cli/printer.ts — generates the CLI table output for metrics, byte-savings, timings, etc. It currently uses manual string padding and toFixed/concat; it needs to switch to toLocaleString for all numeric columns.

• lighthouse-core/report/formatter.js — the legacy HTML formatter that embeds metric values, file sizes, durations, percentages, etc., into the report HTML; it also relies on toFixed calls or string concatenation that should become toLocaleString.

• lighthouse-core/report/handlebar-helpers.js — defines Handlebars helpers (e.g. {{fileSize}}, {{millisecond}}, {{number}}) which are used by report templates and partials to inject formatted numbers; these helpers currently use toFixed and manual code paths and must use toLocaleString instead.

• lighthouse-core/report/v2/renderer/util.js — the new v2 renderer’s utility library (formatBytes, formatMilliseconds, etc.) which formats byte sizes, percentages, and numeric details; these functions currently use Number.toFixed or integer division and need to adopt toLocaleString to automatically include thousands-separators and proper fractional handling.

Updating these four modules ensures that every number you see in the CLI or HTML reports will automatically respect the locale’s separators and fraction-digit settings by routing all formatting through toLocaleString.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a series of JavaScript console logs illustrating how Number.prototype.toLocaleString(undefined, {maximumFractionDigits: X, minimumFractionDigits?: Y}) automatically inserts the locale’s thousands-separator and applies correct rounding/truncation of fractional digits in one call. For example, 2445.8311 with maximumFractionDigits:1 becomes "2,445.8", and a tiny fraction like .000001 rounds down to "2,445" (unless you also specify minimumFractionDigits). The bug request is to adopt this single toLocaleString call everywhere in Lighthouse’s output (CLI tables, HTML report, KB/AUDIT values, element counts, etc.) so that user-facing numbers are consistently formatted with separators and appropriate decimal precision.
